instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of jasmine rice under cold water until it runs mostly clear. Transfer it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups of water and bring it to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on until you serve.
Meanwhile, slice the chicken into thin bite-sized strips. Trim the green beans and cut them into 1 inch pieces. Cut the lime leaves into very thin strips.
Put the oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-low heat. Add the 3 tbsp curry paste and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant. Keep stirring, since the paste burns easily.
Turn the heat to high. Add the chicken and stir constantly for 1 minute, until it's coated in the paste.
Add 2 tsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar and 2 tbsp water. Stir-fry for 2 minutes, until the chicken is no longer pink on the outside.
Add the green beans and 2 tbsp water. Stir-fry for 3 minutes, until the beans are bright green and tender-crisp.
You're cooking the chicken to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check a piece there. No thermometer? Cut a piece open: it's done when there's no pink left.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the lime leaves. Taste it, and add a splash more fish sauce if it's flat.
method_notes: The lead (Eating Thai Food, 4.8 from 8) has too few ratings, so this is a fallback lead. It fries the paste in a little oil on low heat, stir-fries the chicken on high with fish sauce and sugar, and adds the beans last. Thai Foodie (a 5.0 from 1) agrees and adds a longer marinade in oyster sauce, which is left out because oyster sauce can contain wheat. Green beans are used instead of long beans and cook a little longer, and the amounts are scaled up from 1 to 2 servings to 4. Red curry paste is the dish, so choose a mild brand for children.
